name: Indexed lines, base = 100
reader_question: How have series of different sizes changed relative to a common starting point?
relationship: Each series rebased to 100 at one stated base period, so relative change is comparable and level differences drop out.
use_when: Series share a period set but differ greatly in level
Relative change since a stated base period is the question
avoid_when: Absolute levels matter — use small-multiples or annotated-line
A series is zero or negative at the base period

data_contract.notes: Unit of the raw values the index is computed from
Position of the base period in periods; every series equals 100 there
Raw values, one per period; the renderer computes the index

units: Index points, base = 100 at the stated period; the base period and the raw unit are printed on the slide.

editable: Line chart with embedded workbook holding the computed index (Edit Data)
not_data_bound: The workbook holds index values, not the raw values; changing raw data means recomputing the index
End labels and the base-100 reference line are positioned shapes and text, not chart elements

table_alternative: A table of raw values and index values by period for each series.
variations: Rebasing at a policy date instead of the first period
Index with the raw end values in a side table
limitations: The choice of base period changes every line's shape
An index conveys relative change only and hides which series is larger

excluded_alternatives.reason: Two axes invite false visual correlation between series of different size
Large series flatten small ones and hide relative change
